{{Quote|Just give me something to shoot at.|Gloyd|<ref name="precipice" />}}
'''Gloyd''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Houk/Legends|Houk]] [[Officer/Legends|officer]] in the [[Sith invasion fleet|navy]] of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]], and later one of the top ranking members of the [[Lost Tribe of Sith]]. Gloyd was originally a member of a [[Gloyd's brigand crew|crew]] of [[Pirate/Legends|brigands]], who stumbled across the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] Empire while searching for treasure in the [[Stygian Caldera]]. While most of his team did not survive their discovery, Gloyd's experience as a foot [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] and [[Gunner/Legends|gunner]] made him useful to the Sith Empire, and he eventually became a gunnery officer in the Sith [[Navy/Legends|Navy]]. Gloyd served under [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Yaru Korsin]] on the [[Sith dreadnaught]] ''[[Omen]]'', and the two became lifelong friends. In [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], on a [[Mining/Legends|mining]] mission to a [[Phaegon III's largest moon|moon]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Phaegon III]], the ''Omen'' was [[Skirmish over Phaegon III|attacked]] by [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], causing the ''Omen'' to veer off course as it jumped to [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] and crash-land on the remote world of [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]]. After several harrowing nights trapped in the [[Mountain/Legends|mountains]], the ''Omen''{{'s}} crew made it to civilization, where they posed as the [[Skyborn|gods]] of the native [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] and took over the planet. Despite Gloyd's best efforts, no way off the planet could be found, and he instead served for [[Standard year/Legends|years]] at the side of his friend Korsin, now [[Grand Lord]] of the Lost Tribe of Sith. In [[4975 BBY]], Gloyd and Korsin were [[Duel near the Kesh Sith Temple|attacked]] by a force led by Yaru's [[Marriage/Legends|wife]] [[Seelah Korsin|Seelah]], who wanted to avenge the [[Death/Legends|death]] of her former husband [[Devore Korsin|Devore]] [[Duel near the Omen|at Yaru's hands]] and to install her son [[Jariad Korsin|Jariad]] as Grand Lord. Gloyd was killed during the fighting, setting off a [[Proton detonator/Legends|proton detonator]] he had kept for the previous twenty-five years, instead of falling to his enemies. The explosion also gravely wounded Seelah, and her plot was soon foiled.

==Biography==
===Bandit turned naval officer===
{{Quote|Commander.''"<br />"''Not really happy here, Gloyd.''"<br />"''Then you'll want to hear this. As I see it, we've got three choices. We get these people off this rock in whatever will fly. Or we look for cover and hide until they all kill one another.''"<br />"''What's the third choice?''"<br />"''There isn't one. But I figured it'd cheer you up if you thought there was.''"<br />"''I hate you.''"<br />"''Great. You'll make someone a fine Sith someday.|Gloyd and Yaru Korsin, after the crash of the ''Omen''|<ref name="precipice" />}}
[[File:Lost_Sith_Tribe_world.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The mountains of Kesh, where the ''Omen'' crashed in 5,000 BBY]]
The [[Houk/Legends|Houk]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] known as Gloyd was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] in the era before the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]]. Originally a member of a [[Gloyd's brigand crew|team]] of [[Pirate/Legends|brigands]], Gloyd led the life of a [[Gunner/Legends|gunner]] and foot [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]], doing combat with [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] many [[Time/Legends|times]] along the way. At one point, Gloyd found himself on the wrong end of a Jedi's [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], which just missed [[Sai cha/Legends|taking his head off]] and permanently scarred his face. Gloyd's crew eventually learned of the mysteries of the [[Stygian Caldera]] region, which was generally avoided by outsiders. Figuring something wondrous had to be there, they journeyed forth, only to discover the might of the hidden [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]]. While most of his team was wiped out, Gloyd survived and eventually became a member of the Sith Empire's [[Sith invasion fleet|Navy]], rising to the rank of gunnery [[Officer/Legends|officer]]. By [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], Gloyd was the gunnery officer on the<ref name="precipice" /> [[Sith dreadnaught]]<ref name="crosscurrent">''[[Crosscurrent]]''</ref> ''[[Omen]]'', leading his own [[Missile/Legends|torpedo]] crew under a [[Captain/Legends|captain]] named [[Yaru Korsin]], who was on his first [[Commander/Legends|command]]. Sharing a similar acidic wit, and an interest in their job uncommon among the other, more ambitious [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], the two became close friends and by 5,000 BBY had worked together on the ''Omen'' for decades. That [[Standard year/Legends|year]], Gloyd accompanied Korsin and the ''Omen'' on a mission to [[Phaegon III]]'s [[Phaegon III's largest moon|largest]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]], in an attempt to [[Mining/Legends|mine]] [[Lignan crystal|Lignan]] valuable to the Sith efforts in the Great Hyperspace War against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. However, a [[Skirmish over Phaegon III|Jedi attack]] caused the ''Omen''{{'s}} sister [[Starship/Legends|ship]], the [[Harbinger (Sith dreadnaught)|''Harbinger'']], to hit the ''Omen'' as the latter jumped to [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]. Bumped off course and ''en route'' to parts unknown, the ''Omen'' ran into a [[Gravity well/Legends|gravity well]] that grievously damaged the ship. When the ''Omen'' reverted to [[Realspace/Legends|realspace]], it was listing toward a mysterious [[Planet/Legends|planet]] named [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]].<ref name="precipice" />

While the ''Omen''{{'s}} [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]] erupted in chaos, Gloyd, although privately worried, remained calm and even smiled and joked with his equally cool-nerved friend, Yaru Korsin. The damaged ''Omen'' eventually drifted into Kesh's [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]], which was found to have breathable air, although Gloyd saw this positive development as just a reprieve from what was to come. In a desperate attempt to slow the ship's descent, Korsin, after consulting Gloyd, [[Telekinesis/Legends|opened]] the ''Omen''{{'s}} torpedo doors with [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], succeeding in his task. However, the ''Omen'' was still destined to crash, and after everyone took cover, the dreadnaught slammed into a [[Granite/Legends|granite]] ridge. Korsin was caught out of position and was thrown forward and nearly impaled on a shattered [[Viewport/Legends|viewport]], and though Gloyd tried to pull his friend to safety, the continuing movement of the ''Omen'' impeded his progress. The ''Omen'' slid to a halt on a precipice high in the [[Takara Mountains|mountains]]&mdash;Gloyd was one of 355 survivors of the disaster, including Korsin. Many had [[Death/Legends|died]], and twenty-one more perished on a perilous journey through a narrow [[Mountain/Legends|mountain]] pass away from the shattered ''Omen'' to a clearing below. After the Sith set up camp, an incident occurred where the ''Omen''{{'s}} elderly [[Navigator/Legends|navigator]], [[Boyle Marcom]], was attacked and killed by Korsin's [[Spice/Legends|spice]]-addicted half-brother [[Devore Korsin|Devore]], who blamed Marcom for the ship's crash. Shaken by the incident, Korsin sought Gloyd's counsel. Gloyd, who had missed the violence, surmised that they only had two choices: to either find a way off-planet, or hide until everyone else killed one another. Gloyd figured that the only chance they had was to force the crew members to follow Korsin's lead, and push aside anyone who would not abide.<ref name="precipice" />

===Life on Kesh===
{{Quote|You know me. I'm built for battle. This peaceful paradise is getting to me&mdash;|Gloyd, to Yaru Korsin|<ref name="paragon" />}}
[[File:Tahv.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The city of Tahv, capital of Kesh]]
Although Korsin decided to follow Gloyd's advice, the situation did not immediately improve for the stranded Sith. The high altitude and bitter cold combined to kill more wounded crew members, and Gloyd was forced to rely on bitter roots for sustenance. Later on, Gloyd witnessed a large [[Unidentified six-legged mammal|six-legged mammal]] vault into the camp, gruesomely killing one of the injured Sith before it could be taken down.<ref name="precipice" /> Salvation for Gloyd and the other Sith came from an unexpected source, as a native [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] woman, [[Adari Vaal]], stumbled across their isolated camp while fleeing from religious trouble. Although her presence was a source of discomfort for Gloyd, Vaal was convinced to help the Sith escape their predicament. Vaal brought the Sith to the Keshiri [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Tahv]], where they posed as the native [[Skyborn|gods]] and earned the complete devotion and subservience of the Keshiri. Gloyd, along with all the other Sith, was feted by the Keshiri, who allowed them to move into homes previously occupied by their ruling council, the [[Neshtovar]]. Once they were settled down, Gloyd set out with Korsin on a mission to dig up metals necessary to repair the ''Omen''. Gloyd first oversaw an effort to clear a new path through to a nearby peninsula, a route needed to bring materials to the ''Omen''. That phase was successful&mdash;however, as they would soon find, the metals they sought were nowhere to be found. For better or for worse, the Sith were stuck on Kesh.<ref name="skyborn">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Skyborn]]''</ref>

Over the next fifteen years, Gloyd continued to faithfully serve his friend, now the [[Grand Lord]] of the new [[Lost Tribe of Sith]], Yaru Korsin. However, Gloyd remained ever anxious to leave Kesh, and frequently pitched different escape plans to Korsin in the new [[Kesh Sith Temple|Sith temple]] built in the mountains at the ''Omen''{{'s}} crash site. In [[4985 BBY]], Gloyd came to Korsin with his latest plan: using one of the ''Omen''{{'s}} surviving boring [[Laser/Legends|lasers]] to fire signals into space, hoping to catch the attention of a passing [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]]. Gloyd's idea was quickly dismissed as ludicrous by Korsin's science [[Advisor/Legends|advisor]], [[Ermon Parrah]], and ultimately rejected by Korsin. Not long after Gloyd's pitch to Korsin, gruesome news rolled into the temple&mdash;the entire population of the southern town of [[Tetsubal]], recently visited on an ecological survey by Korsin's [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith pureblood]] advisor [[Ravilan Wroth]], had mysteriously died. Along with Korsin and his [[Marriage/Legends|wife]] [[Seelah Korsin|Seelah]], the widow of the by-now-deceased Devore, Gloyd rushed to Tetsubal to observe the grisly scene, finding only Wroth alive amidst a sea of Keshiri corpses. Fearing that an airborne biological agent was responsible, Korsin sent a shaken Gloyd back to Tahv, to make sure that his daughter [[Nida Korsin|Nida]] made it safely back to their mountain temple. The deaths in Tetsubal, as well as similar incidents in other nearby towns, were ultimately judged to be caused by Wroth and his compatriots, due to manipulation by Seelah as part of a plot to eliminate the [[Blood/Legends|pureblood]] Sith from the Lost Tribe to open the way for an all-[[Human/Legends|Human]] version. As a result, the Korsins led a wholesale [[Red Sith Purge|purge]] of the forty-five Sith purebloods on Kesh, leaving the Houk Gloyd as the only [[Alien/Legends|non-Human]] remaining in the ranks of the Tribe.<ref name="paragon" />

===Last stand===
{{Quote|Commander, I wouldn't put this one in charge of mucking out the uvak stalls.|Gloyd to Yaru Korsin, referring to Jariad Korsin|<ref name="savior" />}}
[[File:KeshSithTemple.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Kesh Sith Temple, the site of Gloyd's death]]
The deaths at Tetsubal caused a stir amongst the Keshiri, and the Lost Tribe feared that they could lose their support entirely. However, Gloyd was instrumental in retaining the devotion of the natives, thinking up a stunt where a known Keshiri [[Unidentified Keshiri dissenter|dissenter]] was brought to Tahv's [[Circle Eternal]] plaza to proclaim against the Sith, only to suddenly die, mysteriously [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force choke|choking]] to death on his own words. This display of [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] [[Force power/Legends|power]] was a complete success, and with the belief of the Keshiri reaffirmed, the mass deaths of the Tetsubal [[Ragnos Lakes|region]] were effectively passed off as the result of the residents' lack of faith in the divinity of the Lost Tribe. By [[4975 BBY]], with all attempts to find a way off Kesh having failed, the Lost Tribe decided to stay there for good&mdash;with no reason to stay by the ''Omen'', they committed to remove themselves from their mountain temple and live amongst the Keshiri. Their intentions were revealed in a massive ceremony at the site of the Circle Eternal, in front of thousands of cheering Keshiri. An aged Gloyd served as Yaru Korsin's ceremonial [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguard]], personally introducing Adari Vaal, who was feted as the "Daughter of the Skyborn," and lastly [[High Lord]] [[Jariad Korsin]], son of Devore and Seelah, one of the top candidates to succeed Yaru Korsin as Grand [[Lord/Legends|Lord]]. While Jariad was believed to be Korsin's heir, he was not the true choice&mdash;for years, Gloyd had helped Korsin hide his daughter Nida's training in the dark side, which Seelah had tried to suppress, as the Grand Lord groomed her for his position.<ref name="savior" />

Unbeknownst to Gloyd, Seelah and her son Jariad were plotting to overthrow Korsin, as revenge for the death of Devore twenty-five years earlier&mdash;although the circumstances of his death were kept secret, during the Sith's time stranded in the mountains Devore had tried to usurp control of the group, leading to a lightsaber [[Duel near the Omen|duel]] and his death at the hands of Korsin. By chance, the event had been witnessed by Adari Vaal, and it was through her that Seelah learned how her husband had died. For decades she and Jariad planned to kill Yaru Korsin, and they finally struck soon after the ceremony. Unfortunately for Gloyd, he was with his friend Korsin at the time, and they and four bodyguards were [[Duel near the Kesh Sith Temple|ambushed]] as they walked in the temple. Although outnumbered four-to-one and encircled by Jariad and his contingent of [[Sith Saber]] warriors, Gloyd and Korsin resolved to fight. Luckily, they got a timely distraction, as a [[Keshiri resistance]] group, secretly led by Adari Vaal, stole the temple [[uvak]] beasts as part of a plan to destroy the Lost Tribe's hold over their planet. The theft of the uvak gave Gloyd and crew a chance to make a run for it, and make a stand on better ground. Gloyd eventually became separated from Korsin, and was chased into another part of the complex by Seelah's warriors. Gloyd fought back with all his might, ably holding out against wave upon wave of enemies despite his old age. However, his and Korsin's time was running short.<ref name="savior" />

As Gloyd's last stand drew near its end, Korsin played his trump, as Nida Korsin and her [[Skyborn Rangers]] uvak-riding club arrived on the scene as reinforcement, turning the tide of the battle. While Seelah's plan fell apart before her [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], Gloyd brought the fight to her chamber. Cornered, Gloyd knew his time had come, and he wanted to take everyone else with him. Gloyd produced a [[Proton detonator/Legends|proton detonator]], a weapon he had had up his sleeve since the crash of the ''Omen'' twenty-five years earlier. Gloyd set the detonator off, killing himself but bringing the entire room down on his enemies. In the end, Seelah's coup was a complete failure&mdash;Jariad died in combat with Nida and Yaru Korsin, and although Seelah survived, Gloyd's proton detonator had severely wounded her, and she permanently lost the use of her [[Limb/Legends|legs]]. Although Yaru died from his injuries, Nida Korsin lived to take over the Lost Tribe.<ref name="savior" /> By [[3000 BBY]], 2000 years after the arrival of the Sith on Kesh, Gloyd was still remembered amongst the Keshiri and the Lost Tribe. In that era, Gloyd was revered by a [[Politics/Legends|political faction]] known as [[Force 57]], comprised of disfigured Humans who revered the "Fifty-seven" non-Humans of the early days of the Lost Tribe. Gloyd was remembered as a figure to be pitied, the one non-Human that the Korsins let live, like a pet. Gloyd was also remembered in the form of the exclamation "Gloyd's blood!," used most notably by<ref name="pantheon">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Pantheon]]''</ref> Grand Lord<ref name="pandemonium">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Pandemonium]]''</ref> [[Varner Hilts]].<ref name="pantheon" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|You and me, we're about the job. Other Sith are about what's ''next.''<nowiki></nowiki>|Gloyd, to Yaru Korsin|<ref name="precipice" />}}
A massive Houk, Gloyd was a gruff but amiable individual<ref name="skyborn" /> with a lively sense of humor<ref name="precipice" /> and a voracious appetite,<ref name="paragon" /> able to joke even in the most dire of situations. Gloyd had an acidic wit, the only one able to match that of his close friend, Yaru Korsin. Over his years as a bandit and Sith soldier, Gloyd became adept in combat, to go along with his physical strength, and as a gunnery officer he was quite knowledgeable about torpedo systems. Gloyd was completely loyal to Korsin, serving faithfully by his friend's side for decades, and always referring to him respectfully as "Commander." Gloyd's brutish tendencies belied his intelligence and astuteness, and in those early days on Kesh when so much was uncertain, Gloyd proved himself an incredibly valuable advisor to his captain. Unlike other Sith, Gloyd was not concerned with ambitious pursuits, instead focusing on his job, a dedication he shared with Korsin.<ref name="precipice" /> Gloyd could also be extremely imaginative, thinking up dozens of wild plans to facilitate the Lost Tribe's escape from Kesh, although every single one was dismissed as unfeasible.<ref name="paragon" /> In addition, he thought up the idea to kill the Keshiri dissenter through the Force, a move which regained the devotion of the natives.<ref name="savior" /> Gloyd never was truly comfortable on Kesh, used as he was to a life spent in battle,<ref name="paragon" /> and at his end, he proved a resoluteness never to surrender, and a valiance in battle.<ref name="savior" />

==Behind the scenes==
Gloyd first appeared in [[John Jackson Miller]]'s [[2009]] [[eBook]] ''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Precipice]]'', the first in the nine-part [[Star Wars: Lost Tribe of the Sith|''Lost Tribe of the Sith'']] series.<ref name="precipice" /> Gloyd was then featured in the next three installments of the series, [[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Skyborn|''Skyborn'']],<ref name="skyborn" /> [[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Paragon|''Paragon'']],<ref name="paragon" /> and [[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Savior|''Savior'']].<ref name="savior" /> In addition, Gloyd was mentioned in a later installment of the series, [[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Pantheon|''Pantheon'']].<ref name="pantheon" />
